annotationRationale: The focus-directrix definition determines the height of A, while the standard parabola equation and coordinate distance formula produce a quadratic in FV. Solving and checking its roots establishes all possible lengths.
sourceMethod: Follows the official alternative coordinate solution with V at the origin and F on the positive y-axis. Explains the directrix step giving y = 20 - d and verifies that both quadratic roots are geometrically feasible.

review.mathCheck: With \(F=(0,d)\), the locus gives \(x^2=4dy\) and \(y+d=20\). Combining these with \(x^2+y^2=441\) gives \(3d^2-40d+41=0\). Its roots are \((20\pm\sqrt{277})/3\), both in (0,20), so both produce real points satisfying the distances. Their sum is \(40/3\), choice B.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, originally worded adaptation of MAA Q20's coordinate alternative on page 13. It obtains the identical parameter quadratic and explicitly verifies both roots, covering both configurations illustrated on page 12.
review.annotationCheck: The focus-directrix definition and standard equation are appropriately assessed. Directrix/range properties, coordinate distance and quadratic-formula solving are suitable supporting knowledge. Both necessity and realizability are established.
